title: Finite Realizations and Effective Memory in Nonlinear Quantum Filtering
summary: Nonlinear dynamics generate non-Gaussian states and operations, but they also make continuously monitored quantum systems difficult to track. A quantum filter performs this task by compressing a noisy measurement record into a set of evolving variables that predict future observables. For Gaussian dynamics, this compression is exact and finite. In nonlinear systems, conventional moment equations generally expand without bound, but the failure of one representation does not prove that every finite description is impossible.
